items.stem: Why can web analytics undercount visitors?

options.text: Ad blockers, consent refusals and tracking-prevention stop some events from being recorded
options.rationale: Correct: blocked or unconsented tracking leads to under-counting.
That would overcount, and is not the typical issue.

options.text: Analytics tools record a perfect census
options.rationale: They sample and miss blocked events.
Many events are recorded; only some are missed.

items.explanation: Correct: blocked or unconsented tracking leads to under-counting.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when running a web A/B test? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Decide the sample size and run time before starting
Wait for the planned sample before declaring a winner
options.rationale: Correct: stopping early inflates false positives.

options.text: Stop the test as soon as one variant is briefly ahead
options.rationale: Early stopping on noise produces false winners.

options.text: Change the variant mid-test whenever it looks weak

items.stem: A report shows 1,000 users and 1,600 sessions. What does this most likely mean?

options.text: Some users visited more than once, creating multiple sessions
options.rationale: Correct: sessions exceed users when people return.

options.text: The data must be wrong because sessions cannot exceed users
options.rationale: Sessions routinely exceed users through repeat visits.

options.text: Every user had exactly one session
options.rationale: That would make the two counts equal.

options.text: Users and sessions mean the same thing

items.explanation: Correct: sessions exceed users when people return.
